nodes.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be terms of the same type $A$ in the same typing context $\Gamma$. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one left-to-right call-by-value step and $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t' \Downarrow v$, then $t \Downarrow v$.
nodes.title: Big-step evaluation is closed under backward reduction steps

nodes.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be terms of the same type $A$ in the same typing context $\Gamma$. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps and $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t' \Downarrow v$, then $t \Downarrow v$.
nodes.title: Big-step evaluation is closed under backward multi-step reduction

nodes.summary: If a term $f$ of function type $A \Rightarrow B$ in the empty context is a value, then $f$ is a lambda abstraction: there is a term $b$ of type $B$ in the one-variable context $[A]$ such that $f$ is the abstraction of $b$.
nodes.title: Canonical forms for closed function values

nodes.summary: A term $t$ of type $A$ in the empty context is in normal form, that is, has no call-by-value reduction step, if and only if it is a value.
nodes.title: Closed normal forms are exactly the values

nodes.summary: For terms $t$, $t_1$, $t_2$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, if $t$ reduces in one call-by-value step both to $t_1$ and to $t_2$, then $t_1 = t_2$.
nodes.title: Small-step call-by-value reduction in STLC is deterministic

nodes.summary: For every typing context $\Gamma$ and type $A$, if a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ evaluates in the big-step call-by-value semantics both to $v$ and to $w$, written $t \Downarrow v$ and $t \Downarrow w$, then $v = w$.
nodes.title: Determinism of big-step evaluation in the simply typed lambda calculus

nodes.summary: Fix a typing context $\Gamma$. For terms $t$ and $v$ of the same type in context $\Gamma$, the big-step evaluation relation $t \Downarrow v$ is the least relation such that every lambda abstraction $\lambda.\,b$ evaluates to itself, and an application $f\,a$ evaluates to $v$ whenever $f \Downarrow \lambda.\,b$, $a \Downarrow u$ and $b[u] \Downarrow v$, where $b[u]$ is the body $b$ with its newest free variable…
nodes.title: Big-step call-by-value evaluation in the simply typed lambda calculus

nodes.summary: For every type $A$ and every closed term $t$ of type $A$, that is, a term in the empty typing context, there is a term $v$ such that $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-value semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.
nodes.title: Closed simply typed terms have a big-step evaluation

nodes.summary: For terms $t$ and $v$ of the same type in the same typing context, $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$, if and only if $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps and $v$ is a value, that is, a lambda abstraction.
nodes.title: Big-step evaluation is small-step evaluation to a value

nodes.summary: A term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is in normal form when there is no term $t'$ such that $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one call-by-value step.
nodes.title: Normal forms for call-by-value reduction in STLC

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $v$ be terms of the same type in the same typing context. If $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps and $v$ is a value, then $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.
nodes.title: Small-step evaluation to a value implies big-step evaluation

nodes.summary: Every term $t$ of type $A$ in the empty context is either a value or reduces in one call-by-value step to some term $t'$.
nodes.title: Progress for closed STLC terms

nodes.summary: One-step reduction on terms of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is the least relation closed under three left-to-right call-by-value rules: if $f$ reduces to $f'$, then the application $f\,a$ reduces to $f'\,a$; if $f$ is a value and $a$ reduces to $a'$, then $f\,a$ reduces to $f\,a'$; and if $a$ is a value, then the application of the abstraction of $b$ to $a$ reduces to $b[a]$, the result of substituting $a$ for…
nodes.title: Small-step call-by-value reduction in STLC

nodes.summary: For terms of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, multi-step reduction is the reflexive transitive closure of one-step call-by-value reduction.
nodes.title: Multi-step call-by-value reduction in STLC

nodes.summary: For every closed term $t$ of type $A$, that is, a term in the empty typing context, $t$ terminates (it reduces to a value in finitely many left-to-right call-by-value steps) if and only if there is a term $v$ such that $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$.
nodes.title: Termination in terms of big-step evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $v$ be terms of the same type in the same typing context. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step semantics, written $t \Downarrow v$, then $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) left-to-right call-by-value steps.
nodes.title: Big-step evaluation implies small-step evaluation

nodes.summary: A term of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is a value exactly when it is a lambda abstraction.
nodes.title: Values of STLC

nodes.summary: If a term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is a value, then there is no term $t'$ to which $t$ reduces in one call-by-value step.
nodes.title: Values are irreducible

nodes.summary: Every value $v$, that is, every lambda abstraction, of any type in any typing context evaluates to itself in the big-step semantics: $v \Downarrow v$.
nodes.title: Values evaluate to themselves

nodes.summary: In the call-by-value simply typed lambda calculus, if a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ evaluates by big-step evaluation to a term $v$, written $t \Downarrow v$, then $v$ is a value, that is, a lambda abstraction.
nodes.title: Big-step evaluation produces values

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
